nexusClaim.etiologicalTrigger: Documented gastrinoma (the Zollinger-Ellison syndrome alias of this identity) with biochemical confirmation of hypergastrinemia and inappropriate gastric acid hypersecretion - gastrin drives ECL-cell and parietal-cell hyperplasia and sustained maximal acid output, and the resulting ulcer disease is the syndrome's defining complication at locations that may extend beyond the stomach and duodenum.
nexusClaim.mechanismSummary: The tumor's unrestrained gastrin secretion stimulates enterochromaffin-like cell and parietal-cell proliferation with sustained maximal acid output; acid-pepsin injury overwhelms mucosal defense (mucus-bicarbonate barrier, prostaglandin-mediated perfusion, epithelial restitution) and breaches the mucosa into the submucosa as peptic ulceration, conventionally at atypical distal sites in this syndrome; antisecretory proton pump inhibition heals ulcers and prevents recurrence while tumor control removes the gastrin drive - the treatment-response pattern that grounds the obstruction-mechanical and structural-lesion DIRECT precedents.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hormonal hypersecretion cascade: gastrinoma cells secrete gastrin autonomously (loss of normal feedback), circulating gastrin expands the oxyntic mucosa through ECL-cell trophic drive and parietal-cell stimulation, basal and stimulated acid output rise to the upper physiologic range or beyond, and the chronically acidified duodenal and gastric lumens injure the mucosa faster than defenses (bicarbonate, mucus, prostaglandins, mucosal blood flow) can repair, progressing from erosions to full-thickness peptic ulcers; acid suppression collapses the final step (ulcer healing with recurrence only while the drive persists), confirming the chain as a graded causal mechanism documented prospectively in Zollinger-Ellison cohorts.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The causal chain is the defining pathophysiology of the syndrome with prospective treatment-response documentation (antisecretory therapy heals and prevents ulcers; tumor-directed therapy removes the drive), but PROBABLE rather than WELL_ESTABLISHED is used because the supporting series are modest in size (a 72-patient prospective trial and narrative reviews), ulcers in an individual with a gastrinoma can still arise from Helicobacter pylori, NSAID, or stress pathways, and no population-level counterfactual quantifies ulcer incidence attributable to gastrinoma alone; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Biochemical confirmation of gastrinoma (fasting serum gastrin with secretin stimulation if needed, basal and maximal acid output documentation); endoscopic documentation of gastric or duodenal (or atypical distal) ulcer with healing evidence under antisecretory therapy or after tumor treatment; Helicobacter pylori status testing and NSAID or antiplatelet exposure history; chronology documentation dating the tumor's biological presence rather than diagnosis (symptoms precede diagnosis by a median of nine years in the prospective cohort); MEN1/familial context workup; gastroenterology and endocrinology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric or duodenal ulcer
